issues.legal_issue: Full ownership acquired by a Hindu female over property in her possession at the commencement of the succession statute is not defeated by a subsequent adoption to her deceased husband.
material_facts: The widow inherited property from her deceased husband and possessed it when the succession statute came into force.
After the statute came into force, the widow adopted a son and later settled part of the property on her daughter.
The adopted son challenged the settlement, arguing that the adoption related back to the husband’s death and made the widow unable to transfer the property.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent adoption did not defeat the widow’s full ownership or invalidate her settlement; the appeal was allowed and the trial court’s decree was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, property possessed by a Hindu female when the Act commenced is held by her as full owner, not as a limited owner. Section 4(1)(a) makes Hindu law texts, rules, and interpretations cease to have effect on matters for which the Act provides. Accordingly, the Hindu law fiction that adoption relates back to the adoptive father’s death cannot restrict the ownership conferred by section 14(1). The Court approved Yamunabai v. Ram Maharaj Shreedhar Maharaj, AIR 1960 Bom. 463; it referred to Shrinivas Krishnarao Kango v. Narayan Devji Kango, [1955] 1 SCR 1, and Krishnamurthi Vasudeorao Deshpande v. Dhruwaraj, [1962] 2 SCR 813, on the relation-back doctrine, and to Sukhram v. Gauri Shankar, [1968] 1 SCR 476, and S. S. Munna Lal v. S. S. Rajkumar, [1962] 3 Supp. SCR 418, on the effect of the Act on Hindu law rules.

predicates.female_possessed_property_at_statutory_c: A Hindu female possessed the property when the succession statute came into force.
predicates.adoption_occurred_after_commencement: The female adopted a child after the succession statute came into force.
predicates.female_transferred_property_after_adopti: The female transferred the property after making the adoption.
predicates.adopted_child_challenged_transfer: The adopted child challenged the female’s transfer on the basis that the adoption related back to an earlier death.

issues.definition: When a Hindu female possessed property at statutory commencement, later adopted a child, and then transferred the property, her full ownership is not defeated when the adopted child challenges that transfer.
